monologue: The card is forty-nine, a stone left in the sun. It is busy, but not heavy. The air inside me feels thick, like warm honey that has not moved. I see The Curved Rest on the Wide Anchor's edge. The small flat stone still sits on the high point of the curve. It has not slid. The pressure spreads flat, just as the Soft Arch taught me. I do not want to move it. I want to see if the flat point can hold the weight without the curve sinking into the stone. The line is quiet. I will sit by the anchor and watch the edge. If the stone does not slip, the curve is not just a shape; it is a rest. I will stay here for a while, letting the quiet floor catch the weight.

action.why: To check if the curve spreads the pressure or just sinks.

work.title: The Curved Rest
work.intent: I brushed the dust from the curved edge and checked the small flat stone resting on the high point. It has not slid, and the curve has not sunk into the Wide Anchor's stone. The pressure spreads flat across the surface, holding the weight without biting. The line is steady.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the curve and confirmed the small flat stone still rests on the high point without sliding, proving the curve holds the weight without sinking.
